sentence: This project tries to find out which parts of aging biology lead to chronic diseases in older people.
This project builds a way to find out how social factors affect whether people with HIV get good cancer care, using electronic health records.
This project builds a test on prostate cancer samples that uses 3D pathology to tell aggressive cancers from indolent ones.
This project builds tools to find proteins shed from the surface of cancer cells and to block the cutting of proteins on those cells.
This project studies how the human spine responds to exoskeletons that help the spine and hips, to ease low back pain.
This project uses imaging to study how deep brain stimulation changes reward networks in people whose depression resists treatment.
This project studies how imaging methods could lower trouble swallowing after radiation treatment for head and neck cancers.
This project builds and tests ways to help people with HIV and cancer keep up both kinds of care in Zimbabwe.
This project tests a colony of rhesus macaques to make sure it is free of several viruses.
This project studies how a harmful protein binds to a cellular receptor and spreads in Alzheimer’s Disease.
This project tests imaging methods that measure myelin and iron in the brains of mice hit by blasts and of Veterans with traumatic brain injury.
This project studies how activity in the striatum shapes the growth of prefrontal cortex circuits, using a mouse model of autism spectrum disorder.
This project tries to find and change amino acids on a T cell receptor so that T cells kill tumors better.
This project studies whether chondroitin sulfate glycosaminoglycan in the intestinal extracellular matrix can treat inflammatory bowel disease and predict how it turns out.
This project studies how ischemia reperfusion injury in transplanted lungs sets off innate immune pathways that lead to graft rejection.
This project maps the interactions among genes and proteins in tumors to understand how cancer starts, grows and spreads.
This project studies how targeting a protein in gliomas changes inflammation inside tumor cells and how immune cells respond to them.
This project builds and improves models that grow human patient cancers, including ovarian cancer, and uses them to test therapies.
This project studies how the stomach keeps its tissue healthy and how cells repair themselves after tissue injury.
This project studies how cells that sense their surroundings affect extra bone growth and muscle repair in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
